title: Generalised entanglement wedges in three dimensions
abstract: Generalized entanglement wedges (GWs), proposed by Bousso and Penington for gravitating regions in general spacetimes, share many properties of ordinary entanglement wedges, including nesting, monotonicity and strong subadditivity of their generalized entropies. In AdS/CFT, the corresponding properties of entanglement wedges are consequences of the structure of the dual CFT. In this paper we ask whether the properties of GWs have a similar origin. We explore this question in vacuum AdS$_3$ at leading order in $G$. We first show that every GW on a static slice is a union of geodesically convex regions. Each such region is an intersection of ordinary entanglement wedges, so every GW is built from unions and intersections of entanglement wedges. We then use the Crofton formula of integral geometry to write the perimeter of a convex region as the measure of the set of geodesics that intersect it. In AdS$_3$ every geodesic is the Ryu--Takayanagi surface of a boundary interval, so this measure can be written in terms of the von Neumann entropies of CFT intervals. Strong subadditivity of the CFT entropy guarantees that the measure is positive. Monotonicity and strong subadditivity of GWs then follow from simple inequalities between sets of geodesics. The strong subadditivity of GWs is therefore a direct consequence of strong subadditivity on the boundary. Our results further suggest that GWs correspond to subsystems of the CFT that are more general than boundary subregions.
summary: This theoretical paper explores the origin of entanglement properties in generalized entanglement wedges (GWs) within the context of AdS/CFT. By using integral geometry in AdS$_3$, the authors demonstrate that the strong subadditivity of GWs is mathematically guaranteed by the strong subadditivity of the boundary CFT entropy. This reinforces the idea that bulk geometric structures are dictated by the underlying quantum field theory.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether the fundamental properties of Generalized Entanglement Wedges (GWs) in general spacetimes, such as strong subadditivity, originate from the structure of the dual Conformal Field Theory (CFT) in the AdS/CFT correspondence.
main_result: In vacuum AdS$_3$, the strong subadditivity of GWs is shown to be a direct consequence of the strong subadditivity of the boundary CFT von Neumann entropy, suggesting a deep holographic link.
method: The authors employ integral geometry, specifically the Crofton formula, to relate the perimeter of a bulk region to a measure on the space of geodesics, which is then connected to boundary entanglement entropies.
model_or_system: The analysis is performed in vacuum Anti-de Sitter spacetime (AdS$_3$) on a static slice, utilizing the AdS/CFT correspondence where the bulk geometry is dual to a 2D CFT on the boundary.
key_observables: Generalized Entropy ($S_{	ext{gen}}$), von Neumann entropies of CFT intervals, and the perimeter of the geodesic convex regions.
important_parameters: Leading order in $G$ (Newton's constant), and the geometry of $	ext{AdS}_3$.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to vacuum $	ext{AdS}_3$ and assumes the validity of the Crofton formula and the AdS/CFT dictionary for the leading order terms.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the characterization theorem, showing examples of regions that qualify as GWs based on convexity and perimeter relations, and relating bulk regions to the kinematic space $\Gamma$.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the characterization theorem for GWs in $	ext{AdS}_3$, then uses integral geometry to relate bulk perimeters to boundary entropy measures, and finally proves the strong subadditivity of GWs by leveraging the known strong subadditivity of the boundary CFT entropy.
why_interesting: The connection between bulk geometric properties (GWs) and boundary quantum information properties (CFT entropy) is a cornerstone of modern quantum gravity, providing a concrete realization of the holographic principle.
